What you are looking at

This page is built from the platform’s record of every test a student attempted, with the mark, date and time taken on each try, set against the school’s own internal marks in iAspire. Nothing here is estimated — each figure counts actual rows in those records.

The charts below read across all grades at once. Pick a grade from the filter above and they step aside for that grade’s own subject, chapter and test tables.

Click any student in the engagement chart to open their record — attempts, time per test, average mark and every subject mark. Hovering any point or row shows its exact figures.

Summary

Where this comes from
The platform’s test-attempt exports for Grades 6 to 10, one per section and subject. The roll it is measured against is the school’s class list in iAspire, so every student the school lists is counted, whether or not they have signed in.
What it shows
How many of the students on roll in the current selection have attempted at least one test, and how those attempts divide between a first try and later ones.
What it does not show
Whether a test was set as classwork or homework or taken voluntarily, and whether a student who did not attempt was absent or simply never opened the platform.
Who is not in it
One demonstration account (“EB Workshop 1”), which is not a student. Eleven platform names could not be matched to anyone on the class list; their attempts are listed under “not found in the class list” and left out of the percentages.

These attempts come from another grade's file and are not counted in this grade's figures.

Evidence of impact

Across every grade. Click a grade on the chart to open it.

Where this comes from
The same attempt export. Only students who attempted the same test more than once feed this chart.
What it shows
Where a second attempt took students — their mark on the first try against the best mark of their later tries.
What it does not show
Cause. A student who chooses to retake a test is usually one who means to do better, so this is the gain on retakes, not proof that the platform alone produced it.
Who is not in it
Students who attempted every test only once.

Engagement against attainment

Where this comes from
Across the bottom: the number of tests the student has attempted, from the platform export. Up the side: the student's average internal mark — the school's own Mid-Term I marks for 2026–27 as held in iAspire, not EduBrisk marks — averaged across the subjects the student has a mark in.
What it shows
Whether the students putting in practice on the platform are also the students scoring well in school assessments.
What it does not show
Cause, in either direction: students already doing well tend to practise more anyway. The dashed lines are the school’s fixed attainment bands — below 50% Below, 50–69% In line, 70% and over Above expectation — so they stay put when the grade or section changes. There is no fixed line for practice: read how much a student has practised off the bottom axis.
Who is not in it
The six students with no Mid-Term I mark in any subject. Students with no attempts are kept, in the lane on the left.

Class view

Where this comes from
One bubble per student in the selected section. Position is tests attempted against average internal mark from iAspire; colour is the student's average mark on EduBrisk tests.
What it shows
Three things about one class at once — who is practising, who is scoring in school, and who is scoring on the platform.
What it does not show
Time on the platform: no usage export was supplied for this school, so every bubble is drawn the same size. Colour is banded in fifteen-point steps.
Who is not in it
Students with no internal mark. Students with no EduBrisk mark yet are shown as open circles and counted under the chart.

Subject-wise participation

Click a subject to see its tests.

Where this comes from
The attempt export, grouped by the subject each test belongs to.
What it shows
For each subject, how many students on roll have attempted at least one of its tests and how many have attempted none.
What it does not show
How well students did, and whether the chapters attempted match what the class has actually been taught so far.
Who is not in it
Subjects a grade has not been given on the platform — they do not appear at all. Once a section is chosen, subjects no one in that section has attempted are left off the list.

Section-wise participation

Where this comes from
The same export, grouped by the section each student sits in on the class list.
What it shows
Participation section by section for whatever subject or chapter is selected above.
What it does not show
It does not separate a section that was never set the work from one that was set it and did not do it.
Who is not in it
Students whose section is blank on the class list.

Achiever-level participation

Where this comes from
Achiever levels come from the school's Mid-Term I marks in iAspire for 2026–27. With a subject selected, the level is that subject's mark; otherwise it is the average across the subjects the student has a mark in. HA is above 70%, MA 40% to 70%, LA below 40%. They are not derived from anything on EduBrisk.
What it shows
Whether participation differs between higher, middle and lower achievers.
What it does not show
Current standing. The level is fixed from the assessment it was taken from and does not move with platform results.
Who is not in it
Students with no internal mark carry no level, so they sit outside this table — they are still counted everywhere else. Hindi marks are held for only 75 students, so most students have no Hindi level; Artificial Intelligence, IT, Computer Science and Employability Skills use the student's average level.

Cross-test glance

Where this comes from
Every attempt on the tests in the selected chapter. A filled cell holds the best mark of that student's attempts.
What it shows
One row per student across all the tests in a chapter, so the gaps show up in a single view.
What it does not show
How many attempts produced the mark shown, or when it was taken.
Who is not in it
No one. Every student on roll in the selection has a row, whether they have taken anything or not.

Test-wise participation

Where this comes from
The attempt export, grouped by individual test.
What it shows
How many students attempted each test in the current selection, and how many did not.
What it does not show
Whether the test was assigned, and how long students were given.
Who is not in it
Tests nobody has attempted. The export is built from attempts, so a test with none does not appear.
